name: 1.8 V FT232-class USB-serial adapter (DSD TECH SH-U09C2 with its 1.8 V jumper)
spec: FT232 chip, logic level 1.8 V set by a jumper; an FT232R supports break, a CP2102N does not
serves: Pixel 2 (walleye) and other phones with UART on the USB-C SBU pins
note: The 1.8 V jumper is a retailer's claim: not confirmed on the Pixel 2. Check the jumper before connecting: 3.3 V can damage the phone.

name: USB-C passthrough breakout that brings out the SBU pins
spec: USB2 data, CC1/CC2 and SBU1/SBU2 passed through (the stock Pixel 2 cable lacks the SBU and CC lines and does not work)

name: USB-Cereal (google/usb-cereal, soldered edition)
spec: SBU1 = TX, SBU2 = RX, DIP 1.8/3.3 V, orientation-specific, not USB-C compliant; the repository is archived (2023-01-10), not an official Google product
serves: Pixel phones with the UART on the SBU pins
note: Unconfirmed on the Pixel 2. A wrong DIP setting can damage the target; the chip edition matters (FT232R vs CP2102N).

name: The Pixel 2's console on UART: the breakout with the 1.8 V adapter, or USB-Cereal
wiring: USB-C SBU1 (A8) is the phone's TX into the adapter's RX; SBU2 (B8) is the phone's RX from the adapter's TX; ground on A1; 1.8 V; 115200 baud. Orientation unconfirmed for walleye (the Pixel 2 and Pixel 5a are opposite, per bacon.dev). On the phone: fastboot oem uart enable (bootloader unlocked), reboot to fastboot; fastboot oem uart disable turns it off. It gives a log only.
note: Claimed by four sources, never tried on walleye: confirm with a run and its log (--fit-ref) before calling it confirmed.
